solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Killer whale lying back by sea, not large, certainly agile

indicators.note: something lying back is turned over, so the whale's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the killer whale is the orca

indicators.note: not tells us to take the abbreviation for large out of the sea's name

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A killer whale basking near the sea shows off its agility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying back' turns ORCA into ACRO; 'not large' drops L from BALTIC, leaving BATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobatic performer is supremely nimble, so the word describes something agile to a high degree.

clue.text: Display skeleton perhaps as body in flight

parts.note: to air something is to show it off or display it
a skeleton is one kind of frame, hence the 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A museum puts a skeleton on show, posed as if flying.
explanation.definitionFit: The airframe is the structural body of an aircraft, the part that flies once engines are fitted.

clue.text: Asian recipe found in area educated woman covers

indicators.note: covers means the woman's name is wrapped around the letter for area

parts.note: Rita is the title character of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: An Asian dish turns up in a region a learned woman writes about.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a hairdresser who takes an Open University course, so Rita is the educated woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs, made from a recipe of South Asian origin.

clue.text: Corrupt spy chief and others lead for example

parts.note: base means morally low or corrupt
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
et al is the Latin abbreviation meaning and others

explanation.surface: A crooked spymaster and his associates take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a verb for the spy chief, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a common non-precious metal, the class alchemists hoped to turn into gold.

clue.text: More strictly controlled near royal woman

parts.note: near can mean stingy, as can tight
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Security tightens near a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' in the sense of mean with money is TIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tighter regime is one under firmer, stricter control, a comparative adjective in both cases.

clue.text: Painter having drink — something bitter

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea
gall is bile, proverbially bitter

explanation.surface: An artist with a drink that tastes bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was the Russian-French modernist painter known for dreamlike village scenes.

clue.text: Stock set with food as image shows

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: Instructions describing a set jelly as the picture shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, set around pieces of food.

clue.text: Friend takes a minute with soldier making climb over

indicators.note: in a down clue, making something climb turns it to read upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A pal pauses a moment while a soldier scales a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making climb' turns GI upwards to IG in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a friend, used informally in English as a mate or buddy.

clue.text: Up at loch when swimming one finds scented shrub

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about freely, so these are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone up at a Scottish lake finds a fragrant bush while bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when swimming' rearranges UPATLOCH to PATCHOUL, then I is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is an aromatic Asian plant of the mint family whose oil is used in perfume.

clue.text: That which brings stillness on the Dart?

definitions.text: That which brings stillness on the Dart?

parts.words: That which brings stillness on the Dart?
parts.note: the river Dart suggests a calm stretch of water, but the dart is a poisoned one whose coating paralyses its prey

explanation.surface: Something that calms things on Devon's River Dart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a river in Devon, so the surface suggests peace on the water; the real dart is a blowpipe dart tipped with paralysing poison.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American plant extract causes paralysis and was smeared on darts by hunters.

clue.text: Surrender accepted here, many papers reported

indicators.note: reported signals that the word is spoken, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, so reams are many papers

explanation.surface: A news story about a surrender, covered in many newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Germany's unconditional surrender was signed at Eisenhower's headquarters in Reims on 7 May 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: This French city in Champagne is where the German forces signed their capitulation in 1945.

clue.text: Film featuring boy — one as swamp attack victim?

indicators.note: the boy and the one become a victim, swallowed whole by the swamp predator

parts.note: a gator, short for alligator, is the swamp's attacker
a lad is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A movie about a lad who falls prey to an alligator in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The boy is pictured inside the alligator that ate him, sitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiator is Ridley Scott's 2000 epic starring Russell Crowe as a Roman arena fighter.

clue.text: Let in again to study with Cambridge college

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A student is readmitted to study at a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge college' points at the English university, but it is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to allow them entry a second time.

clue.text: Second drink for anonymous person?

definitions.meaning: asking for ... is asking for a further drink
... is the placeholder name for an unnamed person, as on a team sheet

explanation.surface: Ordering a second round for someone whose name nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A further glass is one more, and A. N. Other is the stock British name for an unidentified individual.

clue.text: Poke fun at swimmer thus leading the course

parts.note: to mock is to poke fun at
a turtle is a swimming reptile
so means thus
up means ahead or leading, as in a match

explanation.surface: Teasing a swimmer who is ahead in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a race course for the swimmer, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock turtle soup is a Victorian dish imitating green turtle soup, served as one course of a dinner.

clue.text: Convivial and available for a bash?

definitions.meaning: sociable, fit to be a member of a club
read literally, the word means able to be clubbed, or bashed

explanation.surface: A sociable type, happy to be invited to any party.
explanation.definitionFit: A clubbable person is sociable, and taken literally the word means fit to be hit with a club.

clue.text: Persuaded to include loud supporting character from Dickens's pen

indicators.note: to include means the first word holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: to be sold on something is to be persuaded of it

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in David Copperfield
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Convinced to add a booming supporting role from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts F below HEEP in this down entry; 'pen' looks like Dickens's writing pen but is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepfold is an enclosure for sheep, which is one kind of pen.

clue.text: Have advantage over minion, one much applied to grindstone

parts.note: to edge someone is to get slightly ahead of them
a tool is someone used by another, a minion

explanation.surface: Getting the better of an underling who keeps his nose to the grindstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose to the grindstone' suggests a hard worker, but it is a blade being sharpened.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge tool is a cutting implement such as a chisel, regularly sharpened on a grindstone.

clue.text: One smuggled in under kilt when suspect has to go in haste

indicators.note: smuggled in means the letter for one is slipped secretly in among the rearranged letters
suspect here is an adjective meaning dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Scot sprints off when what is smuggled under his kilt looks dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges UNDER KILT WHEN, and 'smuggled in' slips I in among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To run like the wind is the idiom for moving extremely fast, hurrying away.

clue.text: Parking, not standard, allowed for minor dignitary

indicators.note: not means the standard letters are removed from the front of the word

parts.note: par is the standard score, as in golf
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Parking a car somewhere substandard was allowed for a petty official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not standard' removes PAR from PARKING to leave KING.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinglet is a petty king ruling a small territory, a minor potentate.

clue.text: Scots couple dressing bishop left in pants

indicators.note: dressing means the Scots word goes round the following letters like clothing

parts.note: twae is a Scots spelling of two, a couple
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by many bishops

explanation.surface: Two Scots help a bishop dress, with something left in his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, not underwear here.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang something pants is nonsense or rubbish, which is what twaddle is.

clue.text: Einstein, maybe one having links to time?

definitions.meaning: Einstein's first name, one example of the name
a watch chain, links attached to a timepiece

explanation.surface: Einstein, perhaps, a man connected with the nature of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An albert is a pocket-watch chain named after Prince Albert, and Albert is also Einstein's first name.

clue.text: Country person of vulgar manners, heading out soon

indicators.note: heading out means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a pleb is a common, vulgar person
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A crude countryman heads off any minute now.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a nation on the eastern Mediterranean coast, north of Israel.

clue.text: Fool about to produce explosive component

parts.note: nit is short for nitwit, a fool
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An idiot is about to make something blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Seeds eaten by parrot satisfy

indicators.note: eaten by means the seeds go inside the other word

parts.note: to parrot is to copy, to ape
peas are the seeds of the pea plant

explanation.surface: A parrot gets its seed and is content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' looks like a bird, but it is a verb, to mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify or placate them by meeting their demands.

clue.text: Meat cut up served in excellent sauce

indicators.note: served in means the meat goes inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with I for the figure one

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
cut means the meat loses its last letter

parts.note: loin is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: Chopped meat is served in a fine sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the meat and 'up' reverses what is left; A1 is written AI, the figure one standing as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal garlic mayonnaise, a cold sauce for fish and vegetables.

clue.text: Ladette cunningly keeps doctor engaged in controversy

indicators.note: keeps means the rearranged letters hold the doctor inside
doing something cunningly means twisting it craftily, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A rowdy young woman craftily holds on to a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' gives EATTLED, which 'keeps' the doctor just after its first letter. A ladette is British slang for a loud, hard-drinking young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embattled is beset by conflict or criticism, caught up in a dispute.

clue.text: Thumb small book with two rings binding

indicators.note: binding means the rings are wrapped around the book

parts.note: each ring is the letter O, so two rings give two Os
vol is the short form of volume, a book

explanation.surface: Leafing through a little book held with a couple of rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumb' looks like a verb for leafing through a book, but a thumb moulding is a kind of ovolo.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex architectural moulding; a small one is called a thumb moulding.

clue.text: Leitmotiv used by Keith Emerson

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recurring motif in the music of the keyboard player Keith Emerson.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith Emerson was the keyboardist of the 1970s prog rock band Emerson, Lake and Palmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical phrase tied to a character or idea, a kind of theme.

clue.text: Time to study philosopher in dreary routine

parts.note: to read is to study
John Stuart Mill was the English utilitarian philosopher

explanation.surface: Spending time studying a philosopher becomes a monotonous grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively any wearisome round of work that never seems to progress.
